svg.title: ATtiny85 · components and connections
svg.desc: Top-view vector ATtiny85, four-pin I2C OLED, two buttons, passive piezo, CR2032 holder, SPDT power switch and decoupling capacitor. Port labels and physical DIP pins follow the ArduCade ATtiny85 Pico profile.

g.text: ArduCade · ATtiny85 Pico · 8 MHz internal clock · one 3 V battery
Matching pin names mean the same connection. Numbers after / are physical DIP pins, viewed from above.
The dot marks pin 1. Check the chip orientation.
1 = PB5 / RESET. Keep this pin for ISP.
8 = VCC. 4 = GND. No USB or RAW pin.
PB0–PB4 differ from physical DIP pin numbers.
Use a DIP-8 socket to swap or program the chip.
Use a 3 V-compatible module; follow its printed pin labels.
No 1 kΩ pull-downs: ArduCade uses internal pull-ups.
Left + right together = A. There is no up, down or B.
One CR2032 · positive via switch · negative to GND
Add 100 nF between pins 8 and 4, close to the chip.
Remove the chip from its socket to program it separately.
ISP: RESET / 1 · MOSI = PB0 / 5 · MISO = PB1 / 6 · SCK = PB2 / 7 · VCC / 8 · GND / 4
Front: display, buttons, piezo and socket. Back: battery and switch. Check the mirrored underside.
ArduCade wiring based on the sunyecz06 reference. Buttons changed to active LOW. Not to scale.
